lessons.about: Starts a sketch on a plane or a flat face; here the XZ plane.
Pulls a sketch profile into a solid.
Turns a profile around an axis.
Moves a profile along a path.
Blends between sections: here a square into a circle.
A box from its length, width and height.
A cylinder from its radius and height.
A sphere from its radius.
A ring from its two radii.
Copies in rows and columns.
Copies around an axis.
Copies along a sketch path.
Mirrors bodies across a plane (here YZ).
Drills a hole into a face.
A round tube along a path, optionally hollow.
A box around bodies, with a margin.
Adds a metric thread to a round face (a cosmetic thread).
Fills the cells that bodies enclose: here where the box and ball overlap.
A spring-like coil from its diameter, turns and pitch.
A thin wall grown from an open sketch line to the faces around it.
Walls from open sketch lines, one each.
Raises (or sinks) a sketch on a face.
Marks a place on a part where joints attach.
Closes the sketch; its closed shapes become profiles.
Adds the constraints and dimensions the sketch needs, then finishes it.
Draws connected straight lines; click point after point, Esc to stop.
A rectangle from two opposite corners.
A rectangle at any angle: one edge, then its width.
A rectangle with rounded corners.
A rectangle from its centre and a corner.
A circle from its centre and radius.
A circle from the two ends of a diameter.
A circle through three points.
An arc from its ends and a point it passes through.
An arc from its centre, start point and sweep angle.
A regular polygon inside a circle.
A regular polygon around a circle (radius to the edge middles).
A regular polygon from one of its edges.
A slot from the centres of its round ends and its width.
A slot from its overall ends and its width.
A sketch point (for holes, references and constraints).
Drives a size: the rectangle's bottom edge becomes 60 mm.
Turns curves into construction geometry (references, not profiles).
A line from its middle and one end.
An arc that leaves the end of a line smoothly.
A circle of a given radius touching two curves.
A circle touching three curves: here the triangle's inscribed circle.
A slot from its centre, one end and its width.
A curved slot through three points.
A curved slot from its centre and ends.
An ellipse from its centre, major axis and minor radius.
A smooth curve through the points you click.
A smooth curve pulled by control points.
A degree-5 control point curve (smoother bends).
A conic curve between two ends, pulled toward an apex.
Marks a line as a centerline (an axis, never part of a profile).
Text as outlines you can extrude or cut.
Applies the constraint the geometry nearly has: the almost-flat line becomes horizontal.
Copies a body's edges into the sketch, linked to them.
Where a body crosses the sketch plane, as linked curves.
Brings 3D edges into the sketch, flattened onto its plane.
Projects another sketch's curve onto a face.
The curve where two bodies meet.
A turned body's outline, drawn in the sketch.
A curve that runs along a face's own grid.
Fits lines and arcs to a mesh's cross-section.
Makes a line horizontal or vertical.
Joins two points: the lines now meet.
Makes curves touch smoothly: the circle rests on the line.
Makes two lines or circles the same size.
Makes two lines parallel.
Makes two lines square to each other.
Pins geometry where it is.
Puts a point on the middle of a line.
Gives two circles the same centre.
Puts two lines on one line.
Mirrors two items about a line (here the sketch's Y axis).
Makes two curves meet with matching curvature (G2).
Makes a closed chain of lines a regular polygon.
Adds the constraints and dimensions until the sketch is fully defined.
Like AutoConstrain, measuring positions from a datum point.
A smooth curve joining the ends of two curves.
Rounds the corners where sketch curves meet.
Cuts a corner off at equal distances.
Cuts a corner off at a distance and angle.
Cuts a corner off at two distances.
Copies curves at a distance, linked to the originals.
Removes a piece of a curve between crossings.
Lengthens a curve to the next one.
Splits a curve where it crosses another.
Resizes sketch geometry about a point.
Moves (or copies) sketch geometry.
Brings a DXF drawing in as sketch curves.
Brings an SVG drawing in as sketch curves.

lessons.about: Puts a reference picture on a plane to trace over.
Sticks a picture onto a face.
Changes a canvas: its size, angle and opacity.
Shows curvature as a comb along curves or faces.
Finds the smallest radius of curvature.
Shows a face's own grid lines.
Where bodies balance.
Stripes that show how smoothly faces meet.
Colours faces by their draft angle for moulding.
A shiny reflection to judge surface quality.
Shows which faces a tool can reach from a direction.
Colours faces by their curvature.
Checks how smoothly faces meet along their edges.
A surface filling a loop of curves.
A flat surface on a sketch region (or a loop of edges).
Gives a surface thickness, making a solid.
Pulls curves into a surface (walls, no caps).
Turns curves around an axis into a surface.
Moves curves along a path into a surface.
A surface blending between sections.
Copies faces at a distance as a new surface.
A strip of surface running out from edges.
A smooth surface bridging two edges.
Sews surfaces that share edges into one body.
Grows a surface past its edge.
Cuts a surface with a plane, keeping one side.
Fills a face's holes back in (as a surface).
Takes a body apart into separate surfaces.
Turns a surface over (its normal flips).
Smooths a free-form surface's shape (its panel; a face with control points is needed).
Rebuilds a surface's edge to meet another surface.
Mirrors sketch geometry about a line.
Copies sketch geometry around a centre.
Copies sketch geometry in rows and columns.
Rounds edges: here the plate's front top edge.
Bevels edges at a distance.
Joins, cuts or intersects bodies: the pin is cut out of the plate.
Resizes bodies by a factor.
Removes faces and heals the gap: the hole disappears.
Moves faces along their normals; neighbours follow.
Hollows a solid, removing the faces you pick.
Tilts faces for moulding.
Divides a face in two along a plane.
Cuts a body in two along a plane; neither half is new material.
Pushes or pulls a face: the top rises by 8 mm.
Moves and turns bodies (here a copy, moved and turned 30°).
Moves a face onto a plane: the top goes up to 25 mm.
Moves a body so one face meets another.
Removes bodies from here on in the timeline.
Rebuilds every feature in the timeline.
Deletes a feature: the fillet goes.
Changes a design parameter: the block follows its width.
Gives a body a physical material (for mass and looks).
Colours a body (or faces).
A plane parallel to another at a distance.
A plane turned about an axis.
An axis through a cylinder's centre.
An axis square to a face, through a point.
An axis where two planes meet.
An axis through two points.
An axis along a straight edge.
A construction point at a corner.
A point where two edges meet.
A point where three planes meet.
A point at the centre of a circle or sphere.
A point where an edge passes through a plane.
A point part way along an edge.
A plane halfway between two faces.
A plane through two edges.
A plane through three points.
A plane touching a round face.
A plane square to an edge, part way along it.
A plane through a line, square to another plane.
Bends a wall up from a sheet edge.
Covers a sheet with a hole pattern.
Folds a sheet edge back on itself.
Bends a sheet along a line.
Turns a plate into a sheet metal body.
Lists the flat pattern: size, outline and bends.
Lays the bends flat.
Folds an unfolded sheet back up.
Makes or edits a sheet metal rule (thickness, bend radius…).
A screw boss on the inside of a case.
A lip around a case's rim, to locate its lid.
A snap-fit hook.
A raised rest pad.
Makes or edits a plastic rule (wall, draft, clearance…).
Gives bodies a plastic rule.
A new component (a part of the assembly).
Places another design as a linked component.
Connects two parts with a joint (here a slider), then moves it.
A joint between parts where they already are.
Makes parts move together as one.
Moves a joint to a value: B slides 15 mm.
Ties one joint's motion to another's.
Makes two turning joints mesh like gears.
A turning pinion drives a sliding rack.
A cylindrical joint whose turn drives its travel, like a nut on a thread.
A cam turning drives a follower along its profile.
Turns contact sets on: parts stop instead of passing through each other.
Every part takes part in contact.
Turns contact off.
A contact set: these parts can't pass through each other.
A motion over time, from key values of joints.
Traces a point's path as a joint moves.
An exploded view: parts pushed apart.
Keeps parts where you moved them.
Puts moved parts back.
Finds where bodies overlap, and how much.
A bill of materials: the parts and how many.
Volume, area and size of bodies (the numbers appear below).
Cuts the view open on a plane to see inside.
Makes a configuration table column from a parameter.
Shows the configuration table.
Inserts a standard fastener.
Inserts a STEP file's bodies as a component.
Inserts a mesh file (STL, 3MF, OBJ, glTF) as mesh bodies.
Saves bodies as an STL or 3MF mesh (for printing).
Rebuilds a scanned or STL mesh of a mechanical part as editable faces.
Builds a prismatic mesh again as a sketch, an extrusion and its holes, with a parameter for each size.
Reads a scanned mesh as the stack of layers it was modelled from and builds it again as a sketch and an extrusion per level.
Cuts a mesh into silhouettes along a direction and lofts a solid through them, for a shape that is no stack of layers.
Reads a mesh as the surfaces it stands for: planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori, each certified against the mesh itself. Nothing is changed.
Renders a realistic image of the design (in the Render workspace).
Lists what the renderer will draw.
A cone or a truncated cone from its base circle, height and top.
A plane through an axis and a point off it.
Puts points that divide a curve into equal lengths, and keeps them spaced as it changes.
A curve from formulas for x and y over a range of t.
Scales, turns and moves sketch geometry in one step.
What the sketch holds and whether it is fully defined (the numbers appear below).
Leaves a sketch without keeping what changed since it was opened; one Undo brings it back.
A frame member along each line of a sketch, in the section you choose.
Walls and bends along a path drawn across a sheet edge.
Replays the history from the marker to the end, a step at a time.
Gives each component a colour of its own, without changing its appearance.
Brings a scanned point cloud (.ply, .xyz, .pts) into the design as points.
Saves the bodies and opens them in your 3D-printing slicer.
Reopens a finished sketch to change it.
Draws a line across the whole view, as a reference rather than an edge.
A reference line through two points; it guides geometry without becoming an edge.
A reference line straight across, through a point.
A reference line straight up, through a point.
A reference line at an angle from the sketch's X.
A reference line parallel to a curve, through a point.
A reference line square to a curve, through a point.
A reference line from a point, touching a circle.
A reference line touching a circle where you pick it.
A reference line touching two circles.
A reference line halving the angle between two curves.
Lines drawn through points anywhere in space, not on one plane.
A smooth curve through points anywhere in space.
An arc through three points in space.
A point anywhere in space, to build on.
Copies sketch geometry, with the constraints among it.
Takes sketch geometry out, ready to paste elsewhere.
Puts copied sketch geometry back, where you choose.
Writes the flat pattern as a DXF for the cutter.
Writes the bends, their angles and radii as a table.
Turns bodies into components of their own.
Leaves the component being edited and returns to the assembly.
A component's mass, volume and centre of mass (the numbers appear below).
Moves one placement of a component, leaving the others where they are.
Pins a placement where it is, so joints and drives move the rest.
Reads linked designs again and brings in what changed.
Keeps a linked component's geometry and stops following its file.
Where a joint can take a point, over its whole travel.
How far a joint may move or turn.
Changes which bodies in a contact set are kept from passing through each other.
The contact sets in the design (the list appears below).
Whether anything in a contact set is touching or overlapping now.
Shows a configuration without switching to it.
What each configuration sets, as rules you can read and edit.
The standard parts available to drop into a design.
Puts a standard part (a screw, a bearing, a nut) into the design.
Changes a standard part's size to another from its table.
The unit the design shows and measures in.
What the design holds: its features, bodies and sketches (below).
Keeps the view you are looking from, to come back to.
Goes back to a view you kept, or to a standard one.
Gives a kept view another name.
Forgets a kept view.
The views this design keeps (the list appears below).
Remembers the whole design, to come back to with Restore Checkpoint.
Puts the design back as a checkpoint remembered it.
What else would go or fail if a feature were deleted (below).
Moves a parameter in the list, so related ones sit together.
How the parameters depend on one another.
Writes the parameters out as a table.
Reads a table of parameters in, all or nothing.
Where two bodies differ, and by how much (below).
Checks the physical data a material carries.
What your local library holds.
Writes the design's materials and appearances out as a library.
Takes a material or appearance from the library onto what is selected.
Frames the whole model, or just what is selected.
Back to the view a design opens in.
Turns the view to a standard direction: front, top, isometric.
Picks what dragging in the view does: orbit, pan or zoom.
Keeps the model turning, to look it over.
How the model is drawn: shaded, with edges, or as lines alone.
The grid in the viewport, on or off.
A shadow under the model, which says where the ground is.
The navigation bar beside the view, on or off.
Folds the ribbon down to its tabs, for a larger view.
